title: CoQui: A Coordinate-Conditioned Quantum Implicit Generative Adversarial Network for End-to-End Image Generation
authors: Xue Yang, Rigui Zhou, ShiZheng Jia, Dax Enshan Koh, Siong Thye Goh, Young-Wook Cho, YaoChong Li, Xuezhi Ma, Hongyu Chen, Xin Wang
abstract: Quantum generative adversarial networks (QGANs) have attracted increasing attention for image generation using parameterized quantum circuits. Existing amplitude-based approaches face two key limitations: pixel locations are typically encoded by computational-basis indices or address qubits, causing quantum resources to grow with image resolution; meanwhile, jointly decoding many pixels from normalized quantum states introduces probability competition among pixels and limits precise pixel-wise control. To address these issues, we reformulate quantum image generation as coordinate-conditioned implicit function learning. Our method takes spatial coordinates and latent variables as inputs, uses a classical embedding network to generate input-dependent circuit parameters, and evaluates a variational quantum circuit at each coordinate. Pixel intensities are directly obtained from the expectation value of a dedicated color qubit, and a complete image is generated by querying all spatial coordinates. This design decouples image resolution from address-qubit requirements and avoids shared probability-normalization constraints across pixels. We further design a specialized variational quantum circuit to provide structural inductive bias for coordinate-conditioned generation. Simulated experiments on two benchmark datasets show that our method outperforms FRQI-based generation and PQWGAN in visual and quantitative quality while using fewer qubits, and also achieves better generation quality than the corresponding classical baseline.
summary: CoQui introduces a novel Quantum Generative Adversarial Network that models image generation using coordinate-conditioned implicit functions, overcoming the qubit scaling issues of traditional QGANs. By reading out pixel intensities via expectation values at specific coordinates rather than encoding them into circuit amplitudes, it achieves superior performance on benchmark datasets while maintaining structural control over the generated image.
main_problem: The authors address limitations in existing Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks (QGANs) for image generation, specifically the scaling issues with resolution and the probability competition when decoding multiple pixels.
main_result: CoQui outperforms established amplitude-mapping QGAN baselines (like FRQI-based methods) in both visual quality and quantitative metrics while requiring fewer qubits. The method successfully decouples image resolution from address qubit requirements.
method: The core methodology reformulates image generation as coordinate-conditioned implicit function learning, where pixel intensities are read out by evaluating a variational quantum circuit at specific spatial coordinates $(c)$ conditioned on latent variables $(z)$.
model_or_system: The model is CoQui, a QGAN framework built upon Quantum Implicit Neural Representations (QINR). It uses a classical embedding network to generate parameters for a parameterized quantum circuit that maps continuous spatial coordinates and latent codes to pixel intensities via expectation values.
key_observables: Pixel intensity derived from the expectation value of a dedicated color qubit ($\langle Z_0 angle$), evaluated across all spatial coordinates $(c)$. Quantitative metrics include FID, JSD, Entropy, Brightness, and Sobel distance.
important_parameters: The model's structure involves trainable parameters governing circuit layers (e.g., scale $S_l$, bias $B_l$) and the number of feature qubits ($N_f$), which are optimized during training.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that image generation can be accurately modeled as a continuous, coordinate-conditioned implicit function learned via quantum circuits. Limitations include reliance on classical simulation and neglecting realistic hardware noise.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overall CoQui framework (input $ightarrow$ embedding $ightarrow$ VQC $ightarrow$ readout) and show representative MNIST samples comparing Full CoQui against variants lacking key structural components, demonstrating performance gains.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies limitations in existing QGANs. It then proposes the CoQui architecture, detailing its coordinate-conditioned implicit mapping approach. The methodology involves defining the classical embedding network and the complex structure of the variational quantum circuit (including color qubit initialization, data re-uploading layers, entanglement, and residual updates). Finally, it presents quantitative ablation studies and capacity analyses.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes QGANs beyond simple amplitude encoding by adopting an implicit function representation conditioned on continuous spatial coordinates. This structural change addresses fundamental scaling bottlenecks in quantum machine learning for imaging tasks.
